verdict.rationale: Airweave's quickstart has users clone a public GitHub repository and self-host it, so the source is readable. The docs also invite contributing connectors back to the community, and an outside founder places Airweave in the 'open source AI space'. The specific open license is never named in the evidence, so the open-license part of the story rests on implication. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented license (e.g., Apache/MIT) and first-party confirmation of open-source licensing terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: you can build a connector and either use it locally or contribute it back to the community
Always great to have more innovation in the open source AI space
